sections.heading: Overview
sections.content:
The Resistance Band Single Arm Overhead Tricep Extension is a unilateral isolation exercise that targets the triceps, with strong emphasis on the long head, by pressing overhead against band tension one arm at a time.

Training one arm at a time helps address strength imbalances and allows for a greater focus on tricep engagement through the full range of motion.

Anchoring the band under the back foot creates constant, accommodating resistance that increases as the arm extends.

sections.heading: Benefits
sections.content:
- Targets the long head of the triceps through an overhead stretch
- Unilateral training addresses left/right strength imbalances
- Constant band tension for continuous muscle engagement
- Low-impact and joint-friendly
- Improves lockout strength for pressing movements
- Builds overhead shoulder stability and core control
- Portable and easily scalable with band thickness

sections.heading: Muscles Worked
sections.content:
Primary: Triceps Brachii (especially Long Head)

Secondary: Shoulders (Deltoids), Core, Forearms

sections.heading: Set Up
sections.content:
1. Anchor the band securely under your back foot.
2. Adopt a comfortable split stance for balance.
3. Ensure the band has no slack before starting.

sections.heading: Starting Position
sections.content:
1. Place your non-working hand on your hip or thigh to stay still.
2. Grasp the band handle with your working arm.
3. Extend the working arm overhead with the elbow close to the head.

sections.heading: Extension
sections.content:
1. Exhale as you extend your arm upward.
2. Drive through the triceps to full lockout.
3. Keep the elbow tucked and pointing forward.

sections.heading: Return and Repeat
sections.content:
1. Inhale while bending your elbow under control.
2. Maintain tension throughout the rep.
3. Complete reps on one side, then switch arms.

sections.heading: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
- Flaring the elbow outward
- Arching the lower back to press overhead
- Using momentum instead of controlled triceps extension
- Twisting the torso to help lift
- Using a band that is too heavy and breaking form
- Incomplete lockout at the top
- Losing core bracing during the set

sections.heading: Equipment Needed
sections.content:
- Resistance Band with Handle (or loop band)
- Athletic shoes for secure footing
- Optional: Lighter and heavier bands for progression
- Optional: Mirror to monitor form

sections.heading: Band Adjustments
sections.content:
1. Step on the band with your back foot in a split stance.
2. Wider stance creates more tension; narrower stance reduces it.
3. Choose a band thickness appropriate for your strength level.
4. Confirm grip on the handle is secure before starting.

sections.heading: Body Setup
sections.content:
1. Stance: Split stance, back foot anchoring the band.
2. Torso: Tall, ribs down, core braced.
3. Working Arm: Fully extended overhead, elbow near the ear.
4. Non-Working Arm: Hand on hip or thigh for stability.
5. Head: Neutral, eyes forward.

sections.heading: Similar Exercises
sections.content:
- Single-Arm Dumbbell Overhead Extension: Free-weight variation
- Single-Arm Cable Overhead Extension: Cable variation with constant tension
- Two-Arm Band Overhead Tricep Extension: Bilateral variation

- EZ-Bar Skullcrusher: Lying triceps extension

sections.content:
Standing Single-Arm Band Overhead Extension: Described here

Kneeling Single-Arm Band Overhead Extension: Kneeling variation
Tempo Single-Arm Band Overhead Extension: Slow eccentric for hypertrophy
Pause Single-Arm Band Overhead Extension: Pause at the stretch for more tension
Cross-Body Single-Arm Band Extension: Angled variation for different line of pull

sections.heading: If You Have Limitations
sections.content:
Shoulder Mobility Issues: Reduce range or choose a non-overhead triceps variation
Elbow Pain: Lighten the band and keep the elbow tracking forward
Lower Back Issues: Brace the core and avoid arching; try a seated version
Band Too Light: Step wider or use a heavier band
Band Too Heavy: Use a lighter band or narrower stance
Beginners: Start with a light band to learn the pattern
